headline: Reviewed Old Hill and Brigham Street parcel sales and a $745,000 school project appropriation, including a 10 Prospect Street purchase.
summary: The meeting reviewed proposed sales of Old Hill and Brigham Street parcels for new homes. It also reviewed library, public safety, public health, and elder services grants and donations. The $745,000 school project appropriation was scheduled for further review at a separate subcommittee meeting.
decisions: Scheduled the $745,000 school project appropriation order for further review at a separate subcommittee meeting.

decision_evidence.quote: The Committee also reviewed a $745,000 appropriation order related to a school project, including the proposed $645,000 purchase of 10 Prospect Street and two vacant lots using PAYGO funds. The matter was scheduled for further review at a separate subcommittee meeting.

Minutes: 
On July 27, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, met to review 
items scheduled for consideration by the full City Council. The May Revenue versus 
Expenditure Report showed approximately $958 million in revenue and $897 million in
expenditures. Estimated free cash was approximately $12 million, subject to year-end 
adjustments, grant deficits, and the School Department’s net school spending calculation. An 
unaudited year-end report is expected in September. 
 
The Committee reviewed donations and grants supporting library services, public safety, 
emergency preparedness, youth substance use prevention, public health, elder services, and 
infrastructure. These included a $13,000 increase to the Emergency Communications training 
grant, bringing the total to $226,031.30; $30,000 for firefighter equipment decontamination; 
$64,000 for emergency light towers and a shared police and fire mobile command unit; and 
$1,308,213.15 for one supervisor and six officers assigned to the Gaming Enforcement Unit at 
MGM Springfield. DPW rideshare funding will support sidewalks, crosswalks, and ADA 
improvements. Library officials also addressed security concerns and agreed to follow up on 
youth music outreach within the Latino community. 
 
The Committee reviewed the proposed sale of Old Hill parcels to Springfield City of Homes 
Development LLC for three affordable homeownership units. The combined parcels, assessed at 
more than $75,000, would be sold for $7,249.72 as the City’s contribution toward state 
Neighborhood Stabilization Program funding. Brigham Street parcels would be sold to Naylor 
Nation Real Estate for $5,000 and $15,000 for the construction of two market-rate, two-family 
homes. All completed properties would become taxable. 
The Committee also reviewed a $745,000 appropriation order related to a school project, 
including the proposed $645,000 purchase of 10 Prospect Street and two vacant lots using 
PAYGO funds. The matter was scheduled for further review at a separate subcommittee meeting. 
 
 The meeting adjourned at 4:40 p.m.
